> ⚠️ **Preliminary analysis (low confidence)**: treat this as a starting point, not a conclusion.

I don't think this is a code bug in the current build. The same bug was already fixed in `expensify-common`, and version 9.5.10 ships with that fix. More likely, the test accounts don't meet the conditions for short mentions.

**Why the parser isn't the likely cause**
- [At-mentions do not work when user's handle starts with a single character then a dot](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/69685) reported the same symptom and was closed on 2025-10-16.
- The fix landed in [Fix short mention with single character followed by dot isn't recognized](https://github.com/Expensify/expensify-common/pull/881) and [improve shortmention regex to match short prefix(1,2 char) email addr…](https://github.com/Expensify/expensify-common/pull/891).
- App 9.5.10 locks `expensify-common` at `2.0.211`. That version's `shortMentions` regex has both fixes.
- The upstream test still asserts `@j.doe` → `<mention-short>@j.doe</mention-short>` ([`__tests__/ExpensiMark-HTML-test.js:1791-1799`](https://github.com/Expensify/expensify-common/blob/a61b5b46e47e1f5ba0527a20839b3416de4dfeae/__tests__/ExpensiMark-HTML-test.js#L1791-L1799)).

**What a short mention needs to resolve**
A short mention only resolves if all of these are true ([`src/hooks/useShortMentionsList.ts:27-43`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b9a952165248cf929e8f2b6840a679429d57cd25/src/hooks/useShortMentionsList.ts#L27-L43)):
1. The sender's login is on a **private** domain. Public domains such as gmail.com return an empty list.
2. The mentioned user's login is on the **same** domain as the sender's.
3. The mentioned user is in the sender's personal details.

If the check passes, the composer keeps the highlight ([`src/libs/ParsingUtils.ts:23-43`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b9a952165248cf929e8f2b6840a679429d57cd25/src/libs/ParsingUtils.ts#L23-L43)). Sending then expands it to a full mention ([`src/libs/ParsingUtils.ts:72-127`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/b9a952165248cf929e8f2b6840a679429d57cd25/src/libs/ParsingUtils.ts#L72-L127)). I found no rule in this path that limits length or dot placement.

**What I couldn't verify**
- I couldn't run ExpensiMark in this environment. The parser result above comes from reading the regex and the upstream test, not from running it.
- I didn't try to reproduce it in the app. That needs two accounts on the same private domain, and the available test account uses a public domain.

**To confirm**, please share:
- The sender's login and the mentioned user's login, or at least their domains. Do they share the same private domain?
- Whether the failure is in the composer highlight, in the sent message, or both.
- Whether a longer short mention, such as `@john.doe`, works with the same two accounts.

If a same-domain pair still fails, that points to a new cause, and this needs a deeper look.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

This is not a code regression. The Vendor filter was removed on purpose before it reached production, and the regression test case was not updated.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

No new fix is needed on this issue. The work is already in progress:

## Problem Every `Onyx.set` runs `removeNestedNullValues` over the whole value before caching and storing it. The App rewrites some large values repeatedly, especially derived values with one entry per report. On heavy accounts, each Pusher update takes ~350 ms on iOS and Android, and part of that cost scales with the stored value's size rather than the update's. ## Solution (react-native-onyx) 1. Keep the cache free of nulls. This restores the rule from Expensify/react-native-onyx#554 by fixing 4 paths that put nulls in the cache today: batched remove-then-replace merges, lazy SQLite reads, web cross-tab sync, and `Onyx.clear()`. 2. Pass the cached value to `removeNestedNullValues`. It then skips any nested object that is the same object as in the cache. This relies on the shared references kept since Expensify/react-native-onyx#765, and subscribers receive the same values. 3. Add a dev-only alert if App code mutates a cached object in place. ## Behavior change On those 4 paths, subscribers get a missing key instead of `null`. Testing on web and native found this only for `account.errors`, `report.errorFields.export`, and `report.errorFields.notFound`. All three treat `null` and missing the same way. ## Results (heavy account, median before → after) - Each Pusher update: iOS 347→331 ms (-4.6%), Android 349→336 ms (-3.7%), Web CPU x4 326→310 ms (-4.9%) - Incremental reconnect: iOS ~700→~660 ms, Web CPU x4 602→564 ms (-6.6%) - Setting a large object: iOS ~290→~265 ms, Android 293→282 ms - Tested on top of the pending OnyxDerived no-op-write skip, the gain holds: Pusher update 341→316 ms (-7.2%), reconnect 580→532 ms (-5.5%), 5/5 runs faster. - Most of the gain comes from `visibleReportActions`, `sortedReportActions`, and `outstandingReportsByPolicyID`. `reportAttributes` doesn't benefit, because its `undefined` fields break sharing after a full recompute. Fixing that on the App side is a possible follow-up. ## Verify in production In Sentry, `StartupData.Apply` should get shorter for ReconnectApp on heavy accounts (~40 ms on iOS). ## Links - Onyx PR: https://github.com/Expensify/react-native-onyx/pull/856 - Background: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/71205 - Related: https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/98956 _Reported in [Slack](https://expensify.slack.com/archives/C08CZDJFJ77/p1791370922492219)._

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The cost is in react-native-onyx, not in App code. `Onyx.set` calls `removeNestedNullValues` on the entire new value and walks every nested object, even though most of those objects are the same references already held in the cache (shared since react-native-onyx#765). The walk cannot skip them because the cache cannot be trusted to be null-free: four paths still put nulls into it (batched remove-then-replace merges, lazy SQLite reads, web cross-tab sync, `Onyx.clear()`), which breaks the rule from react-native-onyx#554. App only consumes the library through the pinned dependency at https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/37e2b8b8fb247f003796221219ebb979d78cff94/package.json#L204. I did not have the library source in this checkout, so the library-side description below follows the issue and the linked Onyx PR #856.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
- In react-native-onyx, strip nulls on the four paths above (batched remove-then-replace merge, lazy SQLite read, web cross-tab sync, `Onyx.clear()`) so the cache never holds nulls.
- Give `removeNestedNullValues` an optional cached-value argument and return early for any nested object that is `===` to the cached one, since a null-free cached object needs no scan.
- Have `Onyx.set` pass the current cached value into that call.
- Add a dev-only check that warns when App code mutates a cached object in place, since the skip depends on cached objects staying unchanged.
- Add Onyx unit tests: a nested object that is the same reference as the cached one is not traversed, and each of the four paths leaves no nulls in the cache.
- Release react-native-onyx and bump the version in App's package.json (currently 3.0.116).
- In App, check that the only subscriber-visible change is `null` becoming missing for `account.errors`, `report.errorFields.export` and `report.errorFields.notFound`. The issue says all three treat the two the same.
- Optional follow-up in App: stop `reportAttributes` from emitting `undefined` fields so its shared references survive a full recompute.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Skip only the OnyxDerived no-op writes in App: this is a separate fix that already exists, and it does not help when a value changes slightly while most of its nested objects stay the same.
- Keep scanning but cache a "null-free" flag per object: this needs an extra WeakSet lookup per object and is more complex than comparing against the cached reference.

- navigates to Expenses

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
When a user signs up and joins an existing workspace using the **Join my company workspace** onboarding intent (`CONST.ONBOARDING_CHOICES.JOIN_WORKSPACE`), if the workspace has automatic joining enabled and uses the Submit plan, the app unexpectedly navigates to Expenses and opens the workspace's `#admins` room in the Right Hand Panel (RHP / Concierge Anywhere). Since the user is joining an already established company workspace, opening the `#admins` room in the RHP is irrelevant and disruptive.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
In `src/pages/OnboardingWorkspaces/BaseOnboardingWorkspaces.tsx` (lines 146–147, 181–184):
```typescript
const isJoiningSubmitPolicy = policy.policyType === CONST.POLICY.TYPE.SUBMIT;
const shouldUseSubmitFlow = policy.automaticJoiningEnabled && isJoiningSubmitPolicy;
...
if (shouldUseSubmitFlow) {
    navigateToSubmitWorkspaceAfterOnboardingWithMicrotaskQueue(policy.policyID, shouldUseNarrowLayout);
    return;
}
```
1. `shouldUseSubmitFlow` only checks whether `policy.automaticJoiningEnabled` and `policy.policyType === CONST.POLICY.TYPE.SUBMIT` are truthy. It fails to check `onboardingIntent` or `isJoiningCompanyWorkspace` (`onboardingIntent === CONST.ONBOARDING_CHOICES.JOIN_WORKSPACE`).
2. When a user joins an existing Submit workspace via the join intent, `shouldUseSubmitFlow` evaluates to `true` and invokes `navigateToSubmitWorkspaceAfterOnboardingWithMicrotaskQueue`.
3. In `src/libs/navigateAfterOnboarding.ts` (lines 171–173), `navigateToSubmitWorkspaceAfterOnboarding` unconditionally sets `setOnboardingRHPVariant(CONST.ONBOARDING_RHP_VARIANT.RHP_ADMINS_ROOM)` and calls `SidePanelActions.openSidePanel(!shouldUseNarrowLayout)`, forcing the `#admins` room to open.
4. When PR #103652 introduced the `JOIN_WORKSPACE` intent, it did not exclude it from `shouldUseSubmitFlow`.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. **In `src/pages/OnboardingWorkspaces/BaseOnboardingWorkspaces.tsx`:**
Gate `shouldUseSubmitFlow` so that it never applies when joining a company workspace:
```diff
  const isJoiningSubmitPolicy = policy.policyType === CONST.POLICY.TYPE.SUBMIT;
- const shouldUseSubmitFlow = policy.automaticJoiningEnabled && isJoiningSubmitPolicy;
+ const shouldUseSubmitFlow = !isJoiningCompanyWorkspace && policy.automaticJoiningEnabled && isJoiningSubmitPolicy;
```

2. When `isJoiningCompanyWorkspace` is `true`, `shouldUseSubmitFlow` is `false`, falling through cleanly to `navigateAfterOnboardingWithMicrotaskQueue`:
```diff
  navigateAfterOnboardingWithMicrotaskQueue(
      isSmallScreenWidth,
      isBetaEnabled(CONST.BETAS.DEFAULT_ROOMS),
      conciergeReportID,
      reportNameValuePairs,
      policy.automaticJoiningEnabled ? policy.policyID : undefined,
      undefined,
-     false,
+     isJoiningCompanyWorkspace,
  );
```
Passing `isJoiningCompanyWorkspace` as `shouldPreventOpenAdminRoom` guarantees that the `#admins` room is never resolved as the target report across screen layouts, landing the member on Home with the side panel closed.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
- Restricting `shouldUseSubmitFlow` strictly to `onboardingIntent === CONST.ONBOARDING_CHOICES.EMPLOYER`: Rejected to prevent unintended side effects on legacy flows (`LOOKING_AROUND`). Explicitly checking `!isJoiningCompanyWorkspace` is surgical and directly addresses the regression from PR #103652.
- Suppressing the RHP variant inside `SidePanelContextProvider.tsx`: Rejected because treating the symptom inside the side panel provider leaves improper navigation calls firing in the onboarding lifecycle.

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests?
In `tests/unit/pages/OnboardingWorkspacesTest.tsx` (or `tests/unit/libs/navigateAfterOnboarding.test.ts`):
1. User joins an auto-join Submit workspace with intent `JOIN_WORKSPACE`: Verify `navigateToSubmitWorkspaceAfterOnboardingWithMicrotaskQueue` is not called, `setOnboardingRHPVariant(CONST.ONBOARDING_RHP_VARIANT.RHP_ADMINS_ROOM)` is not invoked, and the side panel remains closed.
2. User creates/joins a Submit workspace with intent `EMPLOYER`: Verify `navigateToSubmitWorkspaceAfterOnboardingWithMicrotaskQueue` continues to execute normally.

**Root cause:** Regression from the `@react-navigation/native` 7.3.16 bump (PR #103346). In 7.3.x `useLinking`, the `popstate` handler restores the previous screen only when the browser history entry for the target index carries a stored navigation `state` (`history.get(index)` -> `record.state`); it then either dispatches `goBack()` or `resetRoot(record.state)`. When that stored state is missing, the handler falls into the "treat like a regular deep link" branch: it re-derives state from the path via `getStateFromPath` and resets the root to that, which resolves to Home (or the previous action route) instead of the recorded previous report. Opening reports from the Inbox pushes history entries whose stored state the back handler cannot use, so every browser back drops into the deep-link/reset path.

**Fix approach:**
1. Ensure the navigation integration stores the full navigation state with every browser history entry pushed on report navigation (`history.push/replace({path, state})`), so the back handler's `record.state` branch restores the previous report.
2. As a safety net, when a one-step back finds no stored state for the target entry, resolve the target from the app's own previous navigation state instead of resetting to the deep-linked/Home route.
3. Keep native behavior untouched (no browser history involved on native apps).

**Verification:** (1) On web staging, open several reports from the Inbox, press browser back multiple times then forward - every step lands on the expected report and the URL matches the displayed screen. (2) Single back from a deep-linked report still works. (3) Existing navigation/linking unit tests pass; add a regression test driving `window.history` back/forward across report navigations.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

When a user shares a large video from the Gallery, the OS delivers the file to the native `ShareActionHandler` module (`src/libs/ShareActionHandlerModule/index.ts`). This native module **copies** the video to an app-accessible temp folder *before* calling the JS callback (confirmed by the `ShareTempFile` type comment: "Path to the file copy in the app folder"). Only after that copy completes does the JS layer in `ShareRootPage.handleProcessFiles` (`src/pages/Share/ShareRootPage.tsx`) run the size check:

```
getFileSize(tempFile?.content).then((size) => {
    if (size > CONST.API_ATTACHMENT_VALIDATIONS.MAX_SIZE) {   // 24 MB
        setErrorTitle(...)
```

For files ≤ ~119 MB the copy succeeds, the callback fires, and the async size check correctly shows "file too large." For files > 125 MB the native copy exhausts process memory (or the device I/O buffer) **before** the callback ever fires, crashing the app. The JS validation code is never reached.

The exact threshold aligns with documented native platform memory constraints for app processes receiving share intents on both Android and iOS.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

The fix belongs in the **native** `ShareActionHandler` module:

1. Before copying the file, read the file-size metadata only (via `ContentResolver.query(uri, SIZE)` on Android, or `NSFileManager.attributesOfItem` on iOS). This is a cheap metadata-only call — it does not buffer the file.
2. If the size exceeds `CONST.API_ATTACHMENT_VALIDATIONS.MAX_SIZE` (currently 24 MB), invoke the callback immediately with a special error payload (e.g., a `{error: "FILE_TOO_LARGE"}` flag) instead of attempting the copy.
3. In `ShareRootPage.handleProcessFiles`, handle that error flag by calling `setErrorTitle` / `setErrorMessage` with the "file too large" strings, exactly as the async JS size check already does.

This ensures the "file too large" error is shown before any memory-intensive operation is started, matching the expected behavior described in the issue.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **JS-only guard**: `getFileSize` uses `RNFS.stat()`, which is a metadata call and does not copy the file. It could theoretically be called before `processFiles`. However, on Android the share intent delivers a `content://` URI, and `RNFS.stat` cannot resolve that without the native module first making the file accessible. A JS-only guard is therefore not reliable cross-platform.
- **Increase `MAX_SIZE`**: Not a fix — the crash is memory-related and would simply shift the threshold.

## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
When sharing a large video file (>125 MB) through the native system share sheet on iOS or Android, the app crashes before redirecting the user into the app or showing the file size limit alert.

### What is the root cause of that problem?
The crash happens because both platforms try to load the entire shared video into memory at once in native code before the React Native layer or JS validation ever gets a chance to run:

1. **iOS (`ShareViewController.swift`)**:
In `ios/ShareViewController/ShareViewController.swift` (lines 189 and 201), `handleURLData` loads the entire file into memory using `NSData(contentsOf: url as URL)` before saving it with `fileData.write(to: filePath)`. iOS App Extensions run under strict Jetsam memory limits (often capped around 30MB to 120MB depending on the device). Allocating 125MB+ of raw data in user space triggers an immediate Jetsam termination (`EXC_RESOURCE RESOURCE_TYPE_MEMORY`), killing the extension before it can call `openMainApp()` (`new-expensify://share/root`) to reach `ShareRootPage.tsx`.

2. **Android (HybridApp)**:
As shown in the crash log (`Bug7284638_1791871090289.log.txt`), during `Activity.onResume`, the share intent handler in `yapl.android.misc.InternalStorageUtils.saveUriToStorage` calls `kotlin.io.ByteStreamsKt.readBytes()`. For files over ~119 MB, allocating a single contiguous 135 MB byte array exceeds the available JVM heap headroom (growth limit 256 MB). This throws an unhandled `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError` on the main thread and crashes the app immediately.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?
1. **iOS (`ios/ShareViewController/ShareViewController.swift`)**:
In `handleURLData`, I propose removing the in-memory `NSData` read and using a direct filesystem copy instead:
- Replace `NSData(contentsOf: url as URL)` and `fileData.write(to: filePath)` with `FileManager.default.copyItem(at: url as URL, to: filePath)` (removing any existing destination item first).
- Because `copyItem` operates at the filesystem level, it streams the data on disk without buffering the file in memory, easily staying well within Jetsam memory limits regardless of file size.
- Once the copy finishes, `openMainApp()` fires as normal, redirecting into `ShareRootPage.tsx`. The existing `getFileSize()` check then catches the oversized file and displays the expected `translate('attachmentPicker.attachmentTooLarge')` error alert.

2. **Android (`Mobile-Expensify` wrapper)**:
In `InternalStorageUtils.saveUriToStorage`:
- Replace the unbuffered `readBytes()` call with a buffered stream copy like `input.copyTo(output)` using an 8KB buffer (matching the pattern used in `Expensify/App` at `android/app/src/main/java/com/expensify/chat/utils/FileUtils.kt:63`).
- Another clean safeguard is checking `OpenableColumns.SIZE` upfront via `context.contentResolver.query(...)` before starting the copy.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)
I looked into validating the file size directly inside the iOS Share Extension and showing a native alert dialog there. However, the expected behavior described in the issue is to redirect the user into the main app and show the in-app error modal. Doing a streaming copy on disk allows the native extension to hand off cleanly to the existing `ShareRootPage.tsx` flow without memory spikes.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

Search report rows pass the whole report object, including `report.errors`, to the shared row base. That base renders `item.errors` as a separate red-dot (RBR) line under every row.

- [`ListItemPressable.tsx:111-117`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/components/SelectionList/ListItemComposed/ListItemPressable.tsx#L111-L117) wraps the row in `OfflineWithFeedback` with `errors={item.errors}`. Its default `onDismissError` does nothing, so the X can't clear the error.
- [`SearchUIUtils.ts:2871-2872`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L2871-L2872) spreads `...reportItem` into the row. Transaction rows already avoid this with `errors: undefined` ([`SearchUIUtils.ts:1957`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L1957)).
- The violations line in [`ExpenseReportListItem.tsx:419-450`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/components/Search/SearchList/ListItem/ExpenseReportListItem.tsx#L419-L450) only checks violations and never reads `errors`.
- Inside the report, nothing reads `report.errors`. For DEW, the backend's `DEW_SUBMIT_FAILED` action shows as grey system text that can't be dismissed.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

1. **Remove the below-row error.** Set `errors: undefined` on the report row in `getReportSections`, matching transaction rows. Do the same in the Merge reports item builder ([`SearchReportsMergeReports.tsx:116-122`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/pages/Search/SearchReportsMergeReports.tsx#L116-L122)), which uses the same row base.
2. **Show one message on the row.** In `getDescription`, read errors from the live report first, then the snapshot (`reportForViolations?.errors`, [line 184](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/components/Search/SearchList/ListItem/ExpenseReportListItem.tsx#L184)). Change the early return at [line 434](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/components/Search/SearchList/ListItem/ExpenseReportListItem.tsx#L434) so the line also shows when only errors exist. Join only the sentences that apply. Add `reportViolations.reportFailedToSubmit: 'Report failed to submit because of errors.'` to every locale. The existing violations sentence already ends with a full stop.
3. **Show the full, dismissible error in the report.** Pick the most recent `DEW_SUBMIT_FAILED` action, or else the latest `SUBMITTED` action. Pass `report.errors` into its `ReportActionItem`, following the existing `linkedTransactionRouteError` pattern ([`ReportActionItem.tsx:155`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/pages/inbox/report/ReportActionItem.tsx#L155)). Add a `clearReportErrors(reportID)` action that merges `errors: null` into the report, and call it from that action's `onClose`.
4. **Clear stale errors on retry.** Add `errors: null` to the report in the optimistic data of `submitMoneyRequestOnSearch` and `submitReport`. Today, no submit or approve flow clears `report.errors`.

<details>
<summary>Investigation details</summary>

- Search submit failure writes a generic error to `report_<id>.errors` and removes the optimistic `SUBMITTED` action ([`Search.ts:1654-1665`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/libs/actions/Search.ts#L1654-L1665)).
- Pay, approve, and export failures from Search write the same generic error to the same field ([`Search.ts:577-583`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/libs/actions/Search.ts#L577-L583)). The team should decide whether those failures also use the "failed to submit" sentence or a more general one.
- `report.errors` also forces the row action to View ([`SearchUIUtils.ts:2163`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/9d187260ff527cc0de020927bd59da1b9b7c326d/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L2163)). Clearing the error from inside the report brings back the normal action.
- `DotIndicatorMessage` removes duplicate messages, and the App writes only one generic string. So several lines for one report means the backend sent distinct DEW messages in `report.errors`. I couldn't confirm the backend payload.
- Changing the shared `ListItemPressable` default is riskier, because many other `SelectionList` rows rely on `item.errors`. Changing the data is more targeted.

</details>

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Add an opt-out prop to `ListItemPressable` (for example, `shouldShowErrorMessages={false}`) and set it in `ExpenseReportListItem` and `SearchMergeReportsListItem`. This works too, but it differs from how transaction rows already hide errors.

**Related issue:** [Spend - Error message appears below report row on Merge reports and cannot be dismissed](https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/100499). It has the same root cause, and step 1 fixes it.
